It’s like pieces of something awful keep rising up, but when I try to grasp it, it slips away. I don’t remember much from that time… whole stretches are just blank. I know something happened—must’ve, since I found myself avoiding the news, the basement, even the grocery store on that corner. Anything might set it off, so I stay in most days.

I’ve been hearing voices too—quiet at first, like whispers through a wall. Sometimes they say my name, other times… I can’t be sure. I don’t know if it’s real or just my mind misfiring. My daughter says I talk to people who aren’t here, but I swear I saw my late husband sitting in his chair just last week. He looked real as you. I blinked, and he was gone.

I don’t know if these voices and pictures are from whatever trauma I can’t recall—or if they’re something else entirely. It’s all muddled. This has been going on for about three weeks, I think. More? Less? Time’s been hard to track.
D019-D005_h016.question_a:
I’ve not been myself since my son passed away in that car accident three weeks ago. I keep seeing flashes of the call—finding out, the hospital, people shaking their head—it just hits me out of nowhere, even when I’m folding laundry or trying to sleep. I don’t want to go outside, not even to church. That street where the crash happened? I can’t even look out that window anymore. Sometimes I get in the car and my daughter has to turn around because I start crying or zoning out.  

The worst part is… I can’t remember much about that day. I know they called, but after that—it’s like a fog. Whole chunks are just gone. My mind won’t let me go back there, I think.  

And… well, this might sound strange, but sometimes I hear his voice. Like he’s in the next room, calling “Mama.” But it’s not like I think he’s really here—I know it’s because my heart is broken. It’s always right after I see that image of the police at the door. It’s *him*, it’s *that moment*. I’m not confused, doctor—I know it’s not real. I just miss him so much it feels like he’s speaking. But nothing else feels off. I’m not paranoid, not hearing voices about me, not thinking anyone’s after me. It’s only *him*, only *then*.
D019-D005_h016.question_b:
I’ve been having these awful memories that keep coming back—like my husband’s accident all over again. I can’t get the image of the phone call out of my head; I don’t even remember what they said, just the feeling that something was terribly wrong. Ever since then, I avoid the hospital, his old jacket, even the radio station that was playing that day. I can’t talk about it—part of me feels like I’ve blocked it all out.  

But there’s something else too. Lately, I’ve been hearing my neighbor’s cat talk to me—telling me I’m being watched. It doesn’t sound like a memory—it’s new, clear, like she’s standing in the room. And sometimes I see shadows moving in the hall at night, even when the lights are on. They don’t feel like flashbacks; they’re not about the accident at all. I worry the voices might be plotting with others on the block—I don’t answer the door anymore, not just because of the memories, but because I think they’re coordinating.  

This has been going on for weeks now. The thoughts and sounds, they’re not just about my loss—they feel separate, like they’re building around it. I don’t think it’s grief anymore. Something’s changed.

Something about the eyes in one photo—so hollow—just hit me. I can’t explain it. Since then, certain sounds, even the smell of mildew like in the storage basement, make my chest tighten. But since the break-in at the museum three weeks ago… everything’s changed. I was alone that night when two men ran in, broke a display, and shoved me to the floor. I wasn’t physically hurt, but I can’t stop seeing it—the flashlight beam across the Egyptian sarcophagus, the sound of shattering glass. 

Now, when I walk past certain exhibits, especially at dusk, I feel like it’s happening all over again. I get dizzy, short of breath—like I’m right back there. I avoid going near the east wing altogether. I can remember locking the doors that night clearly, but I can’t recall what one of the men said to me—there’s just a blank spot. 

And… sometimes, I hear glass crack when no one else does. Or I’ll turn around because I swear I see someone in the hallway in a security uniform—but no one’s there.
